rv.q: Gillian Slovo’s play, lifted mostly from survivors’s statements and public records, shines a glaring light from which one cannot hide.
The first act drags, the second act refuses to end, and the cast size, every one of them a protagonist, creates a barrier to empathy.

Gillian Slovo’s proficiency in novel writing gives an added depth to the piece as she weaves together fact and narrative, information and emotion, causing the piece to hit just right and to grip the audience for the full three hour run time.

cn.t: This docudrama about the 2017 London fire ignites strong emotions through survivors' testimony, though critics are mixed on its execution, with some finding the documentary approach powerful while others see structural issues.
